security_contract.positive: Every accepted ScanLimits.output_bytes value bounds the complete compact UTF-8 DoctorReport, including scope, readiness, findings, limits, usage and limitations; usage.output_bytes equals those actual serialized bytes.
security_contract.negative: Untrusted deep paths, JSON-escaped scopes, copied readiness reasons and impossible tiny budgets cannot bypass or weaken the complete-document cap.
controls: A 4,096-byte explicit minimum rejects smaller output budgets with invalid-bound, and a serializer-derived per-scope envelope check rejects larger budgets that still cannot hold their exact scope envelope.
Every Reason path and Finding path is bounded to 4,096 UTF-8 bytes before record construction; overlong paths are omitted rather than approximated or echoed.
Readiness uses fixed pathless limitation guidance instead of copying a limitation outside the payload ledger.

The payload ledger reserves a compact serializer-derived envelope, and finalization measures the real compact document, records that exact byte count, and trims payload with one output-limit reason if needed.

concerns: No full-suite run was performed or claimed: this repair brief permits only scoped doctor/resource bootstrap tests, and the orchestrator owns the later integrated full gate.

Secrets scanning, dependency scanning and fuzz/property infrastructure were inventoried as outside this scoped doctor repair; no dependencies, CI, deployment path or external service boundary changed.
T11 still owns CLI dispatch and public human/JSON rendering. This repair governs the compact DoctorReport representation exercised by Task 9 without expanding into those consumers.
The 2,000-file/16 MiB p95/RSS acceptance benchmark, persisted timing interface, real external database/cache services, native runner execution and dynamic probes remain outside this repair scope.
